prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.

worlds.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. It barred a tenant from suing over rent until his lease expired, and most leases then ran ten more years. The county court's ledgers list almost no rent suits in the 1840s, while those for 1848 and 1849 list more than any earlier pair of years, most repeating complaints tenants had first raised in 1837, and the clerks marked most of them settled by the usual bargaining within two years. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
worlds.explanation: The law blocked suits until leases expired ten years later, and the old complaints then came back and were settled, so it "deferred" the conflict. "Entrenched" fails because the returning suits were settled within two years. "Channeled" fails because the suits went to the same county court once allowed, and "escalated" fails because the returning complaints were the old ones, settled by the usual bargaining.

entrenched.quote: settled by the usual bargaining within two years
entrenched.why: A conflict resolved soon after it resumed had not been made lasting.

channeled.why: The suits returned to the court that had always heard them, so the law opened no new course for the conflict; it only shut the old one for a time.

escalated.quote: repeating complaints tenants had first raised in 1837
escalated.why: The conflict came back in its old form, not sharpened.

worlds.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. It turned each family's tenancy, at that year's rent, into a title that heirs would inherit and that no court could alter, though either side could sue to enforce it. The county court that had always heard rent suits went on hearing about as many each year as before, and its ledgers show the grandchildren of the 1838 parties filing the same suits in 1900, none ending in a new agreement. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
worlds.explanation: Because the law froze each tenancy into a title no court could alter, the same suits passed down through three generations without resolution, so the law "entrenched" the conflict. "Deferred" fails because the court went on hearing suits every year from the start. "Channeled" fails because the suits stayed in the court that had always heard them, and "escalated" fails because their number held steady.

deferred.quote: went on hearing about as many each year as before
deferred.why: Suits continued without a pause, so nothing was postponed.

channeled.quote: The county court that had always heard rent suits
channeled.why: The disputes stayed in their old venue rather than being directed into a new one.

escalated.why: A steady number of suits means the conflict lasted without intensifying.

worlds.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. It created a county board as the only lawful place to contest a rent, and required the landowner to answer at the board's next sitting. Sheriffs' reports that had recorded dozens of blocked roads and burned hayricks in 1837 record almost none after 1839, while the board's minutes list hundreds of petitions a year, close to the number of incidents the sheriffs once counted, until both lists dwindle after grain prices fell. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
worlds.explanation: Roadblocks and burnings gave way to roughly as many petitions before the new board, so the law "channeled" the conflict into a new course. "Deferred" fails because landowners had to answer at the next sitting. "Escalated" fails because the number of petitions matched the earlier incidents, and "entrenched" fails because both lists dwindled once grain prices fell.

deferred.quote: answer at the board's next sitting
deferred.why: Grievances were heard promptly, so nothing was put off.

escalated.quote: close to the number of incidents the sheriffs once counted
escalated.why: The amount of conflict stayed about the same; only its form changed.

entrenched.quote: both lists dwindle after grain prices fell
entrenched.why: The conflict faded with prices rather than being made permanent.

worlds.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. It let a landowner evict a tenant behind on rent without any court hearing, and the 1838 harvest failed. Sheriffs' reports for 1837 record a handful of rent petitions to the county court and no violence; those for 1839 and 1840 record hundreds of evictions and nearly as many blocked roads and burned barns, and they return to the level of 1837 within a year of the law's repeal in 1841. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
worlds.explanation: Once evictions needed no hearing, a few petitions turned into hundreds of evictions answered by roadblocks and burnings, so the law "escalated" the conflict. "Deferred" fails because the change came in the very next year. "Channeled" fails because the law removed the court route and the conflict spilled into the roads, and "entrenched" fails because things returned to the 1837 level soon after repeal.

deferred.why: The conflict sharpened at once rather than being postponed.

channeled.why: The law took away the orderly route, and protest spilled out of it rather than being directed into one.

entrenched.quote: return to the level of 1837 within a year
entrenched.why: A conflict that subsided once the law was repealed had not been made lasting.
